title: Linux 0.11 to 1.0 source evolution
baseline: Historical source tags v0.11, v0.12, v0.95, v0.98, v0.99 and v1.0. Claims distinguish code presence from default enablement and release maturity.

claims.claim: Linux 0.11 already implements executable-backed demand loading; it is inaccurate to say all process pages are eagerly loaded.

Linux 0.12 get_free_page invokes swap_out after allocation scanning fails; try_to_swap_out writes dirty pages to swap and discards clean pages; this source does not implement a resident swapd daemon or second-chance LRU.
v0.12 TASK_SIZE is 64MiB and NR_TASKS is 64; the source compile-time check validates aggregate 4GiB task slots, not 4GiB per process.
v0.95 is an early VFS integration stage; the release note explicitly limits claims about completeness.
v0.99 fs/filesystems.c registers MINIX, EXT, MSDOS, PROC, NFS and ISO9660 conditionally.
v0.98 contains TCP/IP source files, but its release note says TCP/IP was not in the standard boot image and had not yet been fully tested.
v0.99 source includes NFS filesystem implementation and registration.
v0.99 and v1.0 define TASK_SIZE as 0xc0000000, with an explicit 3GiB user-space comment.
v1.0 defines vm_area_struct and VMA operations and exposes mmap/munmap/vmalloc interfaces.
v1.0 vmalloc manages virtual ranges beginning after high_memory plus VMALLOC_OFFSET and tracks them in vmlist.
